supporting_evidence: IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA SAN FRANCISCO DIVISION
summary: Swearing in of witness Persis Yu, appearances of counsel, and introduction of deposition exhibits.

supporting_evidence: Q. Ms. Yu, can you summarize your educational background? A. Certainly. I received my Bachelor of Arts from Mount Holyoke College in 2004. Q. And what degree did you earn after that?
summary: Academic degrees (Mount Holyoke, Boston College MSW/JD), bar admissions, and initial publications.

supporting_evidence: Q. Ms. Yu, continuing on Page 7, let's detail your employment history from 2012 to 2020. A. During those years at NCLC, my primary focus was student loan debt relief and servicer oversight. Q. Did you regularly review loan servicing agreements between lenders and third-party servicers?
summary: Career at National Consumer Law Center (NCLC), Student Borrower Protection Center (SBPC), expert witness roles.

supporting_evidence: Q. Ms. Yu, let's turn to your relationship with and investigation of Defendant Vervent, Inc. A. Very well. Q. When did you first become aware of Vervent, Inc. in connection with ITT Tech loans?
summary: Role of Vervent Inc. (formerly First Associates) as primary servicer for 45,000 ITT Tech PEAKS loan accounts.

supporting_evidence: Q. Now, Ms. Yu, let's focus on Contract and Policy Negotiations between Vervent and PEAKS Trust. A. Very well. I have reviewed the Master Servicing Agreement and subsequent amendments. Q. I am handing you what has been marked as Exhibit 2, dated March 15, 2016.
summary: Negotiation of Master Servicing Agreement, default fee multipliers (2.5x), exculpatory clauses, acceleration triggers.

supporting_evidence: Q. Ms. Yu, we have been testifying for about two and a half hours. This might be a convenient time. (Recess taken from 12:14 p.m. to 1:16 p.m.) BY MR. GIRARD:
summary: Brief recess for lunch break, off-the-record discussion on document production, marginal stamp copy request.

supporting_evidence: Q. Ms. Yu, returning to Contract and Policy Negotiations on Page 33. A. Yes. As we discussed prior to the break, Section 12 was another heavily negotiated provision. Q. What subject did Section 12 of the Master Servicing Agreement cover?
summary: Re-entry to contract terms post-lunch break: Data retention, 90-day cure periods, billing insert arbitration clauses.

topic: Standard Operating Procedures & Student Loan Servicing
supporting_evidence: Q. Ms. Yu, let's now transition to Standard Operating Procedures and Student Loan Servicing practices on Page 39. A. Very well. I have conducted an extensive review of Vervent's Standard Operating Procedures manual. Q. What specific SOP documents did you examine?
summary: Analysis of SOP-102 (Payment Waterfall), SOP-204 (Forbearance Steering), SOP-309 (Autodialer Collections).

supporting_evidence: Q. Ms. Yu, on Page 47, let's examine Vervent's internal compliance audit reports from 2018. of internal audit reports that are protected by the attorney-client privilege and self-critical analysis privilege. (Discussion off the record.)
summary: Defense counsel objection under Rule 502(b) attorney-client privilege regarding internal audit reports; sidebar agreement.

supporting_evidence: Q. Ms. Yu, let's examine Regulatory Compliance and CFPB Audits on Page 49. A. Yes. In 2019, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau issued a Civil Investigative Demand to Vervent. Q. What was the focus of the CFPB's Civil Investigative Demand?
summary: 2019 CFPB Civil Investigative Demand, State AG enforcement, $3.5M restitution consent order, compliance monitor.

supporting_evidence: Q. Ms. Yu, on Page 56, let's re-enter our analysis of the Financial Relationship with Defendant Vervent. A. Yes. To synthesize our financial findings, Vervent generated $18.4 million in total gross revenue from PEAKS. Q. What percentage of that $18.4 million revenue was derived from late fees and collection commissions?
summary: Re-entry to financial relationship: $18.4M revenue synthesis, default collection commission reliance, adjournment.
